newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan labor impasse eases on health front.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan labor impasse eases on health front.

text.p: Venezuela's prolonged labour strife eased Tuesday as doctors accepted a government pay offer but still voted to remain on strike.

At an eight-hour meeting that ended late Monday, union delegates of the 25,000 public doctors accepted a 164 percent increase in the average take-home pay, including bonuses, to the equivalent of $630 a month. They had asked for $1,000.

The administration of President Rafael Caldera, eager to stonewall union calls for higher wages that would jeopardise its inflation-fighting economic programme, had initially offered an across-the-board 25 percent public-sector wage increase.

The doctors, who began striking on Dec. 27, agreed to maintain staffing at emergency wards but said they would lift the strike only when other pending issues were resolved, including pension benefits and better medical supplies.
On another front of Venezuela's troubled social scene, a strike by university teachers, who walked off their jobs on Jan. 15 asking for a 125 percent raise, remained unresolved.

And on Monday, the country's largest trade union rejected government proposals to reform the outdated social security system, saying it may not take part in a next round of tripartite talks scheduled for Thursday.
